title: Homeopathic Doctor
description: Education and Training: Homeopathic doctors typically receive formal training in homeopathic medicine. Training programs and degrees vary by country, but in many places, they attend homeopathic medical schools or undergo specialized training in homeopathy. Homeopathic Philosophy: Homeopaths adhere to the fundamental principles of homeopathy, including the principle of similars ("like cures like") and the use of highly diluted remedies. They believe that substances that can produce symptoms in a healthy person can be used in a highly diluted form to treat similar symptoms in a person with an illness. Individualized Treatment: Homeopaths conduct detailed consultations with patients to understand their physical, mental, and emotional symptoms. They aim to provide highly individualized treatment plans based on the patient's unique symptom profile. Remedy Selection: Homeopaths select remedies from a wide range of natural substances, including plants, minerals, and animals. These remedies are prepared through a process of serial dilution and succussion (vigorous shaking), which is believed to enhance their healing properties. Minimal Dosing: Homeopathic remedies are highly diluted, often to the point where no molecules of the original substance remain. This extreme dilution is thought to reduce toxicity and side effects while stimulating the body's self-healing abilities.

description: News [out of sync] Images from the Ether exhibition by Mrti Ratniks at the RIXC Gallery The opening of the exhibition [out of sync] Images from the Ether by artist Mrti Ratniks took place on Thursday, March 26, at 6:00 p.m. at the RIXC Gallery, Lenu iela 2. [out of sync] Images from the Ether exhibition features video works created using techniques developed through years of experimental practice, employing a hybrid application of analog and digital video technologies. The works are characterized by a generative, algorithmic approach to composition that involves signal processing and real-time recording sessions. For the processing of analog video signals, specially designed equipment and circuits are used that, to a certain extent, operate outside the standard video parameters. The video works include fragments that attempt to capture the visual manifestations of these threshold states, exploring the relationship between stability and collapse. The exhibition showcases a two-channel video installation in which each video operates autonomously (out of sync), yet simultaneously generates new compositional structures by oscillating between states where something is out of place or out of sync, without ruling out the possibility of spontaneous synchrony. Both videos consist of fragments of identical content featuring representations of three-dimensional geometric figures (cube, tetrahedron, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron). The video fragments were created by manipulating and modifying VHS recordings. One of the works in the exhibition is a 50-minute video based on an audio and video recording of a performance created in collaboration with Clausthome (n, November 9, 2024, St. Saviours Anglican Church, Riga). The video was mixed in real time using multiple signal sources. A computer program with an extensive database of pre-recorded video clips was used for mixing, as well as a computer-connected video mixer with multiple analog signal sources. Material recorded on VHS tapes was used in conjunction with analog video signal modulation equipment. A MIDI interface controller was used to control the computer program. This rather intricate arrangement of signals and equipment allows you to control the desired processes with your fingersby sliding and turning potentiometers, or by turning various switches and buttons on and off. This manual control makes it relatively easy to perform multiple actions simultaneously, which is not always convenient with a computer programs digital interface. The video recording on display is not a direct documentation of the performance. Although it has been shortened, it has not been edited or otherwise altered. During the performance, the video signal was broadcast on nine different TV (CRT) screens. Their varying quality and degrees of wear and tear led to inconsistent interpretations of the signal, a phenomenon amplified by the screens' linear arrangement in a compact group. Clausthomes sound collages are composed of frequencies and rhythmic structures generated by modular synthesizers, electromagnetic-field noise, and fragments from an extensive sound archive containing fascinating sound phenomena discovered while surfing the radio spectrum. These diverse signalshums, pulsating noises, voices, and words that suddenly emerge and collapseare all recombined, filtered, and transformed into carefully crafted sonic images. Thanks to Lauris Vorslavs and irts Radzi (Clausthome), Uis Albi, Raitis mits, and the Art Academy of Latvia Mrti Ratniks works in the fields of audiovisual performance and video art. He studied at the Department of Visual Communication at the Art Academy of Latvia. He has participated in the activities of the electronic art and media centre E-LAB and, since 2000, has been a member of the new media culture centre RIXC, contributing to various collaborative projects and producing graphic design for RIXC publications. Since 1998, he has been a member of the artist group F5 (Famous Five). As part of F5, he has participated in several major international exhibitions, including representing Latvia at the 25th So Paulo Biennial (2002) and the 51st Venice Biennale (2005). For over twenty years, he has collaborated with the group Clausthome to create audiovisual performances. Currently, he is a lecturer in the Department of Audiovisual Media Art at the Art Academy of Latvia and is also pursuing a professional doctorate. The exhibition is on view until May 16, 2026. description: What you'll actually own You turn raw sensor data into surgical intelligence, and that intelligence is the heart of what makes Zooly different. About Zooly Zooly Labs is on a mission to make advanced surgical guidance more accessible for joint replacement surgery. Joint replacement can restore mobility and quality of life, yet surgeons often have limited objective information during the procedure to assess joint behavior and guide decisions. We build AI-guided technology that combines intelligent sensing, real-time data, and decision support with familiar surgical workflows and standard instruments, without large capital equipment. We are an early-stage company building a scalable platform across hip, knee, and shoulder. How we work at Zooly Patient-driven. Design-obsessed. We're an in-person team of curious, driven people who care about getting the details right, because there's a patient on the table counting on us. A few beliefs shape how we build, and this role lives at the center of them. Master your craft. We invest in people who go deep. There is no ceiling that forces a great engineer or designer into management to advance. Go as far into your craft as you want. The patient is why. Behind every procedure is a person counting on the people who built the tools. That is what keeps our standards high and our design work honest. Act like an owner. We take responsibility for our decisions and how we communicate, we think long-term, and we bias toward action. What this role is really like This is a hands-on role at a fast-growing startup racing real deadlines. You will wrangle messy sensor data, engineer features, train and validate models, and then argue honestly about what the results really show. You care as much about leakage, drift, and ground truth as about accuracy numbers. If you want clean benchmark datasets handed to you, this is not the role. If you want to build the intelligence that makes a medical product different, it is. What you'll do Build data pipelines, cleaning and synchronization tools, feature engineering, model evaluation, algorithm validation, visualization, and reproducible analyses. title: Chief Architect - Regulated Systems Healthcare & Payments - TechDome
description: The Job, Stated Plainly Somewhere in your org there's an architecture doc nobody's opened since the kickoff meeting. This role doesn't produce those. Techdome is hiring someone to own the technical spine of an 80+ engineer studio that builds systems handling real patient data and real money not staging data, not a demo environment. The architecture you design this quarter is the architecture you're paged about next quarter. You'll sit in the design review, write the PR that sets the pattern, run the incident retro when something breaks at 2am, and sit across the table from the client who's trusting your judgment over their own instinct. Same person, all four rooms. This isn't a diagramming job with an "architect" title bolted on. If what draws you to architecture is the leverage of being right and present not the authority of a title this is written for you. The Shape of the Work You own the platform, not a slice of it. Service boundaries, data models, API contracts, and the parts of the job nobody puts on a highlight reel encryption strategy, observability, cost curves, the scaling plan for eighteen months from now. All of it traces back to you. The compliance load is real, not theoretical. PHI moves through this system, which means audit logging, access control, tokenization, and encryption in transit and at rest aren't checkboxes they're the architecture. Payment data stays walled off with no exceptions, including the exception someone will eventually ask you to make under deadline pressure. The stack is MERN, end to end, with the infrastructure that keeps it alive in production. MongoDB, Express, React, Node plus containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, and secrets management you've actually operated, not just specified in a doc. You make the trade-off calls and you own what happens after. Monolith or microservices, build or buy, synchronous or event-driven every one of these is a bet, and you're expected to defend it with evidence months later when someone asks why the system behaves the way it does. Your patterns outlast your projects. Code review standards, reference architectures, the default way this studio solves a recurring class of problem you're setting the baseline that other architects and tech leads inherit, whether or not they ever meet you. AI tooling is load-bearing here, not a novelty. Engineers across the studio ship daily with Claude Code, Copilot, and Cursor. We're not looking for someone who's merely used these tools we want someone with a real point of view on how they change what "architecture" even means when a junior engineer can generate a service in an afternoon. You grow people without a reporting line to lean on. Senior engineers become tech leads here through the judgment you demonstrate and the trust you build, not through your position on an org chart. .
